answer: At a harbour the water slaps against hulls and pontoons in a slow periodic rhythm, mixed with gulls and the creak of moored boats, and a device there can prove its place by matching that rhythm against a dock microphone in the same minutes. The period of the waves follows the tide and the wind, so a library recording drifts out of phase within seconds, and a farm far inland hears none of it. A mirror of calm water still laps in its own period, the nectar of a quiet morning changes nothing about the tide, and the terrace of a waterfront cafe hears the same swell a real dock device records.
